articles.title: ElevenLabs in early talks for funding at $33 billion valuation
articles.snippet: ElevenLabs in early talks for funding at $33 billion valuation The Economic Times
articles.text:
Synopsis
The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
Reuters
ElevenLabs , a company building artificial intelligence voice models and agents, is in early discussions for a funding round at a target valuation of $33 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.
ElevenLabs’ annual recurring revenue , an estimate of yearly sales calculated from a shorter time period, is now $700 million, one of the people said. In September, the company said its ARR had reached $600 million.
ElevenLabs declined to comment.
The startup was last valued at $22 billion in September after completing an employee tender offer. The company generally announces valuations at a multiple of 11, in reference to its name.
Abiding by that rule would give ElevenLabs an outsize valuation among its broader peer base, even allowing for the wide variation in the way AI companies are valued and measure ARR. London-based video AI startup Synthesia was valued at $4 billion in January, with about $140 million in ARR, according to a February blog post. French model maker Mistral AI was valued at €21 billion in September, hitting an ARR of $400 million in early 2026.
But investors may be spurred on by Anthropic’s record $107.3 billion initial public offering, which delivered huge windfalls for early backers and reinforced hopes that the current crop of highly valued AI firms can deliver huge returns.
ElevenLabs was formed in London by Polish entrepreneurs Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski in 2022, and makes voice and audio models for realistic-sounding synthetic voices that can be used for games, audiobooks and for interactive AI agents.
Chief Executive Officer Staniszewski has previously said the company may start preparing for an IPO in 2028.
The company also recently launched a product that can flag if audio in a live stream is coming from a human or AI.
“Today you assume that you’re interacting with a human unless it’s proven to be AI,” Staniszewski said in a previous interview with Bloomberg News. “In the future I think it will be the opposite.”

articles.title: FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
articles.snippet:
FrenchFry Acquisitions has agreed to combine with Tavia Acquisition Corp. in a transaction that values FrenchFry at $500 million. FrenchFry equityholders would receive 45 million shares in the combined company, valued at $10 per share for the transaction, plus $50 million in convertible promissory notes.
The post FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:20 AM
FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
FrenchFry Acquisitions has agreed to combine with Tavia Acquisition Corp. in a transaction that values FrenchFry at $500 million. FrenchFry equityholders would receive 45 million shares in the combined company, valued at $10 per share for the transaction, plus $50 million in convertible promissory notes.
Two Businesses Built Around Shared AI Tools
The combined company would operate as FrenchFry Holdings and seek a Nasdaq listing. At closing, it would own FrenchFry AI, a no-code platform that helps sales teams find and contact prospective customers, and Catalyst Holdings, which has developed tools for launching and growing apps and games.
Catalyst plans to fund apps and games in exchange for a share of revenue. FrenchFry also plans to acquire established businesses where it sees opportunities to automate manual sales, marketing or customer service work. The holding company intends to provide its businesses with shared finance, accounting, legal and human resources functions.
FrenchFry AI has generated minimal revenue to date, and Catalyst has yet to make an investment or generate revenue, according to the announcement. The combined company expects to need additional capital to pursue its acquisition and investment plans.
The parties expect the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Tavia shareholder approval, an effective registration statement, Nasdaq listing approval and other closing conditions.
KEY QUOTE
“This is a significant milestone toward completing our business combination with FrenchFry. FrenchFry Holdings is built on one AI layer serving many growth businesses. We believe there are thousands of small to medium-sized companies that can benefit from this platform. As a public company, FrenchFry Holdings expects to have the access to capital it needs to grow FrenchFry.ai and to make Catalyst’s first investments and acquisitions, which can run on its AI agents with minimal added overhead.”
Andy Wiederhorn, Executive Chairman And Chief Executive Officer Of Tavia Acquisition Corp.

Tempus secured $385 million in term loans and $115 million revolving to help fund the Personalis acquisition.
The deal pays Personalis holders roughly $600 million cash and $900 million in Tempus Class A stock.
Borrowing remains contingent on the acquisition closing or being reasonably expected to close within one business day.
Tempus AI entered a senior secured credit agreement on November 25, 2026, providing $385 million of term-loan commitments and $115 million of revolving commitments to help finance its pending Personalis acquisition, according to its Form 8-K .
In a separate November 24, 2026 decision, Tempus elected to pay approximately $600 million in cash and issue approximately $900 million in Tempus Class A common stock to Personalis shareholders. These are financing commitments, not evidence that the full amounts have already been drawn. Initial funding requires the acquisition to have closed or be reasonably expected to close within one business day after funding.
Debt Terms and Funding Conditions
Tempus expects borrowings to fund part of the acquisition consideration and related transaction costs, as well as working capital and general corporate purposes. Ares Capital Corporation is the administrative and collateral agent, Ares Capital Management LLC the lead arranger and bookrunner, and ACF Finco I LP the revolving agent.
Term loans bear interest at either the agreement’s Base Rate benchmark plus 4.50% or its Term SOFR benchmark plus 5.50%; revolving loans use Base Rate plus 2.75% or Term SOFR plus 3.75%. Term SOFR has a 1.00% floor, the Base Rate a 2.00% floor, and interest on the loans is payable solely in cash.
Both facilities mature on the fifth anniversary of the effective date. A springing provision can move maturity to 91 days before Tempus’s 0.75% convertible senior notes due 2030 unless those notes are repaid or converted first or specified liquidity requirements are met.
Certain Tempus subsidiaries will guarantee the obligations, which are secured by substantially all assets of Tempus and those subsidiaries. The agreement includes minimum-liquidity and minimum-revenue covenants. Revolving availability depends on eligible accounts receivable and certain qualified cash, subject to reserves and other limitations, and revolving interest can be charged on a minimum balance even when actual borrowings are lower.
Revised Acquisition Consideration
The cash election uses flexibility described in Tempus’s July 20, 2026 acquisition announcement . The merger agreement priced Personalis at $16.25 per common share, representing approximately $1.5 billion in enterprise value net of Tempus’s existing ownership. Consideration was originally structured as all stock, with Tempus holding an option to pay cash capped at 50% of the consideration and a floating exchange ratio capped at 0.3356 Tempus shares per Personalis share.

articles.title: Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
articles.snippet:
Vena Energy has secured a $113 million green loan from BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered to refinance five operating wind and solar projects in Indonesia. The facility provides fixed-rate financing with maturities of up to 17.5 years for assets with a combined generating capacity of 114 megawatts.
The post Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:31 PM
Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
Vena Energy has secured a $113 million green loan from BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered to refinance five operating wind and solar projects in Indonesia. The facility provides fixed-rate financing with maturities of up to 17.5 years for assets with a combined generating capacity of 114 megawatts.
Wind And Solar Assets Covered By The Refinancing
The portfolio includes the 72-megawatt Tolo Wind Project in South Sulawesi and four solar projects in North Sulawesi and West Nusa Tenggara. Together, the solar projects account for the remaining 42 megawatts. The refinancing gives the operating projects a long-term funding base and makes interest costs more predictable over the life of the loans.
Both banks served as arrangers, hedge counterparties and green loan coordinators. BNP Paribas also acted as facility agent, while Standard Chartered served as account bank.
Vena Energy, the renewable energy arm of Vena Group, has operated in Indonesia since 2019. The company says its local projects support employment, skills development and opportunities for nearby businesses. Across the Asia-Pacific region, Vena Energy reported a 30.5-gigawatt development pipeline as of December 31, 2025, spanning onshore wind, solar and offshore wind.
KEY QUOTE
“This refinancing reflects the strength of Vena Energy’s Indonesian operating portfolio and our ability to optimise the capital structure of established renewable energy assets. By securing long-term financing, we are strengthening the financial position of our portfolio while maintaining a stable funding base for these assets. We value the continued support of BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered, which reflects confidence in the quality of our projects and their long-term performance.”
Ravi Nichani, Co-Head Of Investment At Vena Group

articles.title: Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
articles.snippet:
Blulabs has closed an $80 million asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo, including a $20 million accordion feature. The multiyear facility is secured by receivables and inventory and replaces the supply chain company’s previous trade-finance and factoring arrangements.
The post Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:52 AM
Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
Blulabs has closed an $80 million asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo, including a $20 million accordion feature. The multiyear facility is secured by receivables and inventory and replaces the supply chain company’s previous trade-finance and factoring arrangements.
Blulabs plans to use the facility to support working capital, inventory and the expansion of customer programs. It serves airlines, hospitality businesses, distributors and retailers through a global manufacturing and logistics network. The company is also developing software to give its teams real-time visibility into purchase orders, production schedules, freight routing and inventory.
The financing follows a May 2026 investment led by Lodestone Capital at a $160 million pre-money valuation. Blulabs intends to redeem that investment in spring 2027, which would return full ownership to the Garson family.
KEY QUOTES
“Moving to an institutional banking partner like Wells Fargo is a milestone for Blulabs and for our family. It reflects the scale and discipline of the company, and it shows the market that Blulabs is built for whatever the next 20 years of the supply chain have in store. Our vision is a Blulabs product in every hand, so that it’s impossible to go out into the world without interacting with something we’ve made, moved or delivered.”
Cole Garson, Co-CEO Of Blulabs
“Under the leadership of Marc Garson and his family, Blulabs has grown their supply solutions to serve many leading brands. We are pleased to support Blulabs with a flexible capital solution as the company continues to serve its customers and scale its global platform.”
Rich Schultz, Managing Director At Wells Fargo Capital Finance
“This business has always been about trust. Customers trust us because we solve problems, keep our commitments and stand behind them when markets are difficult. Having Wells Fargo behind us is a recognition of what this family has built, and it gives the next generation the strength to take Blulabs to its next level. As the father and founder of this company, I could not be more proud of this milestone.”
Marc Garson, Founder And Chairman Of Blulabs
“AI is changing how the physical economy works, and we are at the frontier in our market. Pairing that technology with the capital strength of this facility will transform Blulabs in ways that are hard to comprehend through today’s lens. In a short time, we will deliver for our customers at a scale that wasn’t conceivable before.”
Remy Garson, Co-CEO Of Blulabs
